title: Normal arithmetic approximation of a smooth affine closed pair
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $g:V=\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$ a smooth affine morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of finite presentation, meaning $B=A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$ for finite lists. Let $Z\subseteq V$ be closed. For $t\in T$ let $V_t=V\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $Z_t$ its inverse image [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field]. Assume $Z_t$ contains no irreducible component of $V_t$ for every $t$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], and every $z\in Z_\eta$ has $\dim\mathcal O_{V_\eta,z}\ge2$, where $\eta$ is the generic point of $T$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$, an increasing system of normal finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $A_i\subseteq A$ with $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$, and compatible affine schemes $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ smooth of finite presentation over $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, with closed subsets $Z_i\subseteq V_i$, such that for $j\ge i$ the pair $(V_j,Z_j)$ is the base change of $(V_i,Z_i)$ along $A_i\to A_j$, and $(V,Z)$ is its base change along $A_i\to A$. Each $Z_i$ contains no irreducible component of any fibre of $V_i\to T_i$; at every point of $(Z_i)_{\eta_i}$ the local ring of $(V_i)_{\eta_i}$ has dimension at least two. Each $A_i$ is Noetherian and for every $t_i\in T_i$ the maximal-ideal completion of $(A_i)_{t_i}$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The schemes $V_i$ and $W_i=V_i\setminus Z_i$ are Noetherian, quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], the transition morphisms on both systems are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and their inverse limits are respectively $V$ and $W=V\setminus Z$ with the displayed base-change projections. Here an inverse limit means the universal scheme with compatible morphisms to all stages.

source.place: EGA IV4 Proposition 21.14.3(ii), proof: approximation by normal finite type Z-subalgebras and descent of the closed pair; IV3 7.8.3(ii),(iii),(vi),(vii), 8.3.11, 8.5, IV4 17.7.8, and IV2 6.1.4, as cited there. Read in the online English EGA translation; local EGA IV4 WANTED.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-algebra-finite-type-model] to choose a finitely generated integer subring $C\subset A$, a smooth $C$-algebra $D$, and $B\cong A\otimes_CD$. Let $P$ be the set of normal finitely generated integer subalgebras of $A$ containing $C$, ordered by inclusion. It is small as a subset of the power set of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-finite-type-subalgebra-extension], it is nonempty, any two members are contained in a third (apply the node to the ring generated by their two finite generating lists), and every element of $A$ belongs to a member (adjoin it to $C$ first). Thus $P$ is directed and its union is $A$. This union is the ring colimit: compatible maps out of the members define a unique map on $A$ by representatives, with addition and multiplication checked in a common member. Each preliminary model $D_i=A_i\otimes_CD$ is smooth of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition].

source.place: Tag 033C, lemma-normal-goes-up, normal finite-type subrings; Tag 00TP, lemma-finite-presentation-fs-Noetherian, smooth model; EGA IV4 21.14.3(ii), arithmetic approximation paragraph.

proof.text: The ring $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], since $A$ is Noetherian and $B$ is finitely presented. Write $Z=V(b_1,\ldots,b_e)$ with finitely many generators of its radical ideal. Each $b_l$ is a finite sum of tensors $a\otimes d$ in $A\otimes_CD$. Choose one $A_*\in P$ containing every coefficient $a$ in these sums, and let $b_{l,*}\in D_*=A_*\otimes_CD$ be the same sums. Restrict to the directed tail $A_i\supseteq A_*$ and put $B_i=A_i\otimes_CD$, $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, $Z_i=V(b_{1,i},\ldots,b_{e,i})$. The tensor-pushout universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives the canonical identifications $A_j\otimes_{A_i}B_i\cong B_j$ and $A\otimes_{A_i}B_i\cong B$, carrying each displayed generator to its displayed image. It also proves $\varinjlim B_i=B$: maps out of this colimit are exactly compatible maps from $A$ and $D$ agreeing on $C$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] gives $T=\varprojlim T_i$ and $V=\varprojlim V_i$ with these projections. Every tail still covers $A$, so these arguments persist after further restriction.

source.place: Tags 01YW and 01YX, affine scheme limits; explicit finite-generator construction in place of EGA IV3 8.3.11.

proof.text: Each $A_i$ and $B_i$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, so its spectrum is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. At the initial stage $*$ apply [lem-sfb-smooth-closed-fibre-codimension-locus] with $c=1$. It gives a constructible $G_1\subset T_*$ whose inverse image in $T$ is exactly the good-fibre locus of $(V,Z)$. That inverse image is all of $T$ by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] to the qcqs affine system $(T_i)$ and $G_1$, and restrict to a tail on which every $T_i$ maps into $G_1$. The base-change clause of the codimension node now gives fibre-component avoidance at every stage. For the generic-fibre bound, the inclusion $A_i\subset A$ induces an injection $\operatorname{Frac}A_i\to\operatorname{Frac}A$, and the generic fibre of our pair is the field extension of its stage generic fibre. Apply the same codimension node with $c=2$ to this field extension: its reflection implication transfers the assumed bound on every point of $Z_\eta$ to every point of $(Z_i)_{\eta_i}$. No surjectivity of $T\to T_i$ and no pointwise equality of local dimensions after field extension is asserted.

source.place: Tag 05F4, lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible; EGA IV2 6.1.4 and EGA IV4 21.14.3(ii), fibre conditions in the arithmetic model.

proof.text: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is excellent by [lem-trf-integers-excellent]. For a prime $\mathfrak p_i\subset A_i$, put $S=A_i\setminus\mathfrak p_i$; this is multiplicative, contains $1$, and excludes $0$. Apply [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] with base $\mathbf Z$ and finite type algebra $A_i$: the local ring $L=S^{-1}A_i=(A_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak p_iL$, is excellent. By [def-exc-excellent-ring] it is therefore Noetherian and a G-ring. Each $A_i$ is a subring of the domain $A$, integrally closed in its fraction field by step 1, so a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] $L$ is a normal domain, and so are all its localizations $L_{\mathfrak q}$, i.e. $L$ is a normal ring. Since $L_{\mathfrak m}=L$, the G-ring definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] makes $L\to\widehat L$ regular: it is flat, and each fibre $\widehat L\otimes_L\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is Noetherian and, taking the trivial extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, which is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], regular. Regular rings are normal [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]. The completion $\widehat L$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and $L\to\widehat L$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-normal-fibres-noetherian-normal] makes $\widehat L$ a normal ring. It is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat L$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]; a local ring equals its localization at its maximal ideal, so $\widehat L$ is a normal, i.e. integrally closed, domain. This proves the assertion at every stage prime.

source.place: Tags 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent; 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent; 0C23, lemma-completion-normal-local-ring (proof: algebra.tex lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian). EGA IV3 7.8.3(ii),(iii),(vii).

proof.text: The $V_i$ are Noetherian by step 3. Each $W_i=V_i\setminus Z_i$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], and $V_i,W_i$ are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. The maps $V_j\to V_i$ are affine because they are maps of affine schemes. Moreover $W_j$ is exactly their inverse image of $W_i$: on a prime this says that not all of the displayed $b_{l,j}$ lie in it, equivalently not all $b_{l,i}$ lie in its contraction. Apply the open-restriction clause of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] to $W_*\subseteq V_*$ and the already identified limit $V$. It gives affine transition maps $W_j\to W_i$ and $W=V\setminus Z=\varprojlim W_i$ with the required restricted projections. The universal properties here are in schemes, so they give precisely the inverse limits requested in the statement.

Sources: Stacks 05F9 (more-morphisms lemma-dimension-fibres-constructible), 0C23/07QW/07QU (more-algebra), EGA IV2 6.1.4; EGA IV4 21.14.3(ii) only online (WANTED). New node lem-sfb-smooth-closed-fibre-codimension-locus is true. On smooth fibres dim O_{X_s,z} = d - dim closure(z), so the condition holds piece by piece on the finitely many relative-dimension pieces X_d. 05F9 gives constructibility over a Noetherian base. Dimension is invariant under field extension, which gives preservation and reflection, and hence the base-change clause. c=1 is component avoidance. Tested c=0, empty Z or fibre, relative dimension 0, A^1_Z with V(p) and V(p,x). Self-contained, statement-only, not a duplicate (searched 05F9 and codimension+constructible), not a restated clause. Steps 1-3 and 5 check against their cited statements: normal f.g. extension gives directedness; finite tensor coefficients descend Z; pushout and limit-affine-transition give the limits; the 05F4 tail at stage * with c=1 gives avoidance; c=2 is reflected via Frac A_i -> Frac A; W_i are preimages, and the open-restriction clause gives W=lim W_i.
